Header:
**Cholesterol crystal embolism - associated acute kidney injury** is characterized by the obstruction of small renal vessels by cholesterol crystals released from atherosclerotic plaques. These emboli induce endothelial injury, ischemia, and activation of inflammatory pathways within the kidney vasculature.

To further investigate the association between complement activation, endothelial cell activation, and immune infiltration observed in renal arteries, small dermal arteries in additional patients are examined. In this case, a superficial reticular dermis artery is studied.

Waypoints.Name: Structure of the artery
Waypoints.Description: Dermal arteries are organized in layers that maintain vascular integrity and regulate blood flow within the skin. These structures ensure proper tissue perfusion, nutrient delivery, and participation in local inflammatory responses through endothelial activation and leukocyte recruitment.

Waypoints.Name: Complement activation
Waypoints.Description: The complement is a part of the immune system. It can be activated by three different pathways : the classical, lectin or alternative pathway. Here, very few deposition of C1 fragments is observed. Most of the deposition of complement fragments seem to be the product of the activation of the lectin pathway.

Waypoints.Name: Immune infiltration
Waypoints.Description: No lymphocyte infiltration is observed, but some macrophages are detected. However, there is no significant immune infiltration in the superficial reticular dermis artery : the slight complement activation does not seem to be enough to induce it.
